# ui::Theme

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

Everything a theme defines: the palette and accent shades, corner radii, padding and border width, the surfaces, text styles and type ramp, the focus visual, motion, popup behavior, window frame settings, and the three button sets custom controls draw with ([`draw_control_chrome`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome)).

A default-constructed Theme is not usable: button_normal, accent_button_* and the other button visuals have no meaningful default. Always get a Theme from [Theme::light()](#light) or Theme::fluent(palette), also for a class member's default (`Theme theme_ = Theme::light();`, never `Theme theme_{};`).

A [Window](../tree/window.md) owns the active theme ([Window::pin_theme()](../tree/window.md#pin_theme)) and hands it to every element's measure and render. An element with a requested theme draws its subtree with [`with_dark_mode`](#with_dark_mode). The fields are plain data, so an app may take a resolved theme and change single values (metrics, type, motion) before applying it. The role colors are the exception: `colors()` is read-only, and a theme with other colors comes from [fluent(const ThemeColors&)](#fluent) or classic(const ThemeColors&, ...). How each built-in control draws itself in an era (its toggle, slider, field and row-selection looks) is internal to the theme and not public. A copy of a theme carries it along unchanged.

Example: 
```cpp
// A dark Fluent theme with a wider focus ring, applied to a window:
ui::Theme theme           = ui::Theme::fluent(ui::Palette::fluent_dark());
theme.focus_ring_outer_width = 3.0f;
window.pin_theme(std::move(theme));
```

## variant

```cpp
ThemeVariant variant = ThemeVariant::Fluent2
```

The design language the theme draws in, the one its factory built it for. Under high contrast it is the variant whose contrast look this is, so check [`high_contrast`](#high_contrast) too. A custom control reads it to ask "is this Fluent?" before reading [`palette`](#palette).

Example: 
```cpp
const bool fluent = (theme.variant == ui::ThemeVariant::Fluent2 || theme.variant == ui::ThemeVariant::Fluent) &&
                    !theme.high_contrast;
const ui::Color fill = fluent ? theme.palette.card_background_default : theme.colors().field;
```

## high_contrast

```cpp
bool high_contrast = false
```

Whether the theme is a high-contrast one, from a system contrast theme or ThemeMode::HighContrast. Its colors are then the contrast scheme's, and [`palette`](#palette) is left default even under the Fluent variants.

## dark

```cpp
bool dark = false
```

Whether the theme draws light content on a dark background: the dark mode of a variant that has both (Fluent 2, Fluent, Mdl2, Metro), or a dark contrast scheme. Every theme sets it, and the fixed-palette eras are light. A custom control reads it to pick a per-mode value, such as a shadow's alpha or a band color, under any variant. `palette.dark` is set only by [Theme::fluent()](#fluent).

## palette

```cpp
Palette palette
```

The Fluent palette the theme was derived from. Only [Theme::fluent()](#fluent) sets it, so it is filled for the Fluent variants outside high contrast. Every other theme leaves it default, so check [`variant`](#variant) before reading it.

## accent_ramp

```cpp
AccentRamp accent_ramp {}
```

The accent shades the theme was resolved from, the Windows defaults when the theme was not resolved from the system's settings. Controls and apps that need a lighter or darker shade of the accent read it here.

## with_dark_mode

```cpp
std::function<Theme(bool dark)> with_dark_mode {}
```

The same theme resolved light (false) or dark (true), which an element with a requested theme ([Element::set_requested_theme()](../tree/element.md#set_requested_theme)) draws its subtree with. Set by [resolve_theme()](namespace-ui.md#resolve_theme) for the variants that have both. Empty for the fixed-palette eras and under high contrast, where a requested theme is ignored. It resolves the request again, so later edits to this theme are not in its result. An element with a requested theme carries the edits that are not colors (metrics, type, motion) over on top of it.

## focus_ring_outer_width

```cpp
float focus_ring_outer_width = 2.0f
```

outer ring stroke, in DIPs

The two-ring focus visual (render/FocusRing.hpp's [draw_focus_ring()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_focus_ring)): a 2px outer ring in `colors.focus` with a 1px `colors.focus_inner` ring right inside it. The pair fills the [`focus_ring_margin`](#focus_ring_margin) pixels outside the control's bounds. [`focus_ring_margin`](#focus_ring_margin) is how far out the outer ring's outer edge lands, half a stroke beyond its center line.

## spelling_error

```cpp
Color spelling_error = Color::from_argb(0xFFC42B1C)
```

[TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox)'s misspelling squiggle. Defaults to the Fluent light theme's critical red, the red every Windows spell checker uses, which the era themes keep. [Theme::fluent()](#fluent) takes the palette's semantic_fill_critical, a lighter red in dark themes. High contrast uses the window text color, the only one sure to show on the field background.

## disabled_text_effect

```cpp
TextEffect disabled_text_effect {}
```

How a disabled control's text is drawn, on top of `colors.text_disabled`: the text beside a [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox), [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) or [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch), and a disabled [TextControl](../controls/text.md#uitextcontrol). Windows 95 through 2000 draw disabled text the way they draw a disabled push button's label, engraved: a highlight copy offset by a pixel under a shadow copy. So [`Theme::classic()`](#classic) sets the same `Emboss` it gives [`button_disabled`](#button_disabled).

[Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) only. A disabled check mark or radio dot stays a flat gray glyph, so the indicators read their own `text` and never this. Windows 3.x draws disabled text in plain gray, as every non-classic theme does.

For offset and scale moves: [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch)'s knob slide, [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton)'s dot resize, and [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider)'s inner-circle grow/shrink into Normal/Disabled.

## animations_enabled

```cpp
bool animations_enabled = true
```

Whether controls animate at all, resolved from [ThemeRequest::animations](theme-request.md) and the system setting. When false, [resolve_theme()](namespace-ui.md#resolve_theme) also zeroes the durations above and [`popup_motion`](#popup_motion), and [Window](../tree/window.md) ticks its tree with [animations_enabled()](#animations_enabled) false, so every animation the framework plays lands on its end state at once.


How the era's shapes and text are rasterized. [Window::render()](../tree/window.md#render) applies it first, every frame. The default is antialiased shapes, grayscale text and no pixel snapping. Only the classic, Luna and Aero themes set something else.

## overlay_material

```cpp
std::optional<AcrylicBrush> overlay_material {}
```

The material that flyouts, drop-down lists, menus and the other popups that close on an outside click fill with: in-app acrylic, which blurs what is drawn behind it. Only Fluent 2 sets it ([`Palette::acrylic_in_app_default()`](palette.md#acrylic_in_app_default)), and only while the system allows transparency ([`OsThemeSnapshot::transparency_enabled`](os-theme-snapshot.md)) and no contrast theme is on. Unset, those surfaces fill with their solid color, `surfaces.menu`. [fill_overlay_surface()](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#fill_overlay_surface) makes that choice.

## icon_font_family

```cpp
FontName icon_font_family = "Segoe Fluent Icons"
```

The symbol font a control's glyphs are drawn from, passed as the `font_family` of `render/IconGlyph.hpp`'s [`draw_icon`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_icon). Windows 10 Fluent uses `Segoe MDL2 Assets`, and Windows 11 `Segoe Fluent Icons`, a redesign with the same code points. Each theme names its font.

## colors

```cpp
const ThemeColors& colors() const noexcept
```

The colors by role, filled for every era and mode (see [ThemeColors](theme-colors.md)), and what a custom control reads first. Read-only. A different set of colors is a different theme, made by `fluent(const ThemeColors&)` or `classic(const ThemeColors&, ...)`.

## with_content_colors

```cpp
Theme with_content_colors(Color text, std::optional<Color> background = std::nullopt) const
```

A copy of this theme for drawing a container's content. Content in the default text color draws in `text`, and content that reads the background, such as a control that blends into its surface, sees `background` when one is given. A container whose surface differs from the page, such as a card, a popup or an accent-filled box, draws its children with it.

Example: 
```cpp
// An accent-filled box whose text follows the accent:
class AccentBoxControl : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        renderer.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 0.0f, theme.colors().accent);
        child_->render(renderer, context.with_theme(theme.with_content_colors(theme.colors().text_on_accent)));
    }

private:
    std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> child_;
};
```

## generation

```cpp
std::uint64_t generation() const
```

A number unique to this Theme value, never 0. Each theme built, copied or moved into gets a new one, so a cache of measurements or derived themes can tell a new or edited theme from the one it came from. Editing a field in place keeps the number. Hand the edited theme over as a new value ([Window::pin_theme()](../tree/window.md#pin_theme)) for caches to see the change.

## fluent

```cpp
static Theme fluent(const Palette& palette)
```

A Fluent theme derived from [`palette`](#palette): every value above and the built-in controls' own looks.

## fluent

```cpp
static Theme fluent(const ThemeColors& roles)
```

A Fluent theme derived from a full set of role colors. The roles that differ from the Fluent light colors, or the dark ones when `roles.background` is dark, replace the palette colors they come from, and everything else follows from them as in [fluent(const Palette&)](#fluent). Change `accent` alone and the selection, the accent button's hover and pressed fills and the informational severity follow it. `colors()` of the result reads back what was passed for every role that was changed.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ThemeColors colors = ui::Theme::fluent(ui::Palette::fluent_dark()).colors();
colors.accent          = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF8764B8);
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::fluent(colors));
```

## classic

```cpp
static Theme classic(const ClassicPalette& palette, bool hot_track, const char* font_family, bool win3x_edge = false)
```

A classic (Windows 95, 98, 2000) theme derived from [`palette`](#palette), the classic counterpart of [fluent()](#fluent). Every classic theme, a custom scheme included, is one [`ClassicPalette`](classic-palette.md) plus this function, with no hand-assembled [`ButtonVisual`](button-visual.md) per state. `hot_track` lights a button's face under the pointer, as Windows 98 does and 95 does not. `font_family` is the UI font, at 11 px. Name a TrueType font: bitmap fonts can't be loaded, so `MS Sans Serif` or `System` quietly gives Segoe UI. The Windows 9x and 3.x themes pass `Microsoft Sans Serif` and then set it at 8 pt on a 13 px line. `win3x_edge` switches every edge to the Windows 3.x construction in place of the 9x four-ring bevel. Windows 3.x has only face, shadow and highlight colors for buttons, but draws a four-color, uneven edge: a 1px black frame, a 1px white highlight on the top and left and a 2px gray shadow on the right and bottom (`render/Bevel.hpp`'s [`draw_win3x_border`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_win3x_border)). It also rounds the push button, flattens the check box to a black and white outline, marks it with an X instead of a tick, and drops the engraved disabled label.

## classic

```cpp
static Theme classic(const ThemeColors& roles, bool hot_track, const char* font_family, bool win3x_edge = false)
```

A classic theme derived from a full set of role colors, the classic counterpart of [fluent(const ThemeColors&)](#fluent). The roles that differ from the Windows Standard scheme's colors replace the scheme color they come from: `background` and `control_fill` replace the face, and with it the bevel, `text` the face text, and `field` and `field_text` the window colors. `selection`, `selection_text`, `text_disabled`, `link` and `overlay` (the menu) replace their own. The other roles follow from those, as in classic(const ClassicPalette&, ...).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::ThemeColors colors = ui::Theme::classic(ui::ClassicPalette::windows_standard(), true, "Tahoma").colors();
colors.selection       = ui::Color::from_rgb(0x008080);
window.pin_theme(ui::Theme::classic(colors, true, "Tahoma"));
```

## metro

```cpp
static Theme metro(const MetroPalette& palette, bool dark)
```

A Metro (Windows 8.1) theme derived from [`palette`](#palette), like [fluent()](#fluent) and [classic()](#classic). Metro has a dark and a light mode and a user accent, and [`dark`](#dark) says which mode the theme is. Pass [`MetroPalette::metro_dark()`](metro-palette.md#metro_dark) or `metro_light()` with the matching [`dark`](#dark).

## mdl2

```cpp
static Theme mdl2(const Mdl2Palette& palette, bool dark, const Color& accent)
```

An MDL2 (Windows 10, 1507 to 1703) theme derived from [`palette`](#palette), like [fluent()](#fluent), [classic()](#classic) and [metro()](#metro). Like Metro, MDL2 has a dark and a light mode, and [`dark`](#dark) says which, together with the matching [`Mdl2Palette::mdl2_dark()`](mdl2-palette.md#mdl2_dark) or `mdl2_light()`. `accent` is the system's current accent, which this era uses on the controls.

## early

```cpp
static Theme early(const EarlyPalette& palette)
```

An early-Windows (1.x and 2.x) theme derived from [`palette`](#palette), like [fluent()](#fluent), [classic()](#classic), [metro()](#metro) and [mdl2()](#mdl2), and the oldest of the five.

This era has no sense of depth and no button face, selection or disabled-text color, so its colors are an [`EarlyPalette`](early-palette.md). Its whole drawing model is six rules: a 1px frame, a flat fill, reverse video, black-and-white glyphs, fixed-pitch text without antialiasing, and a double 1px frame for a dialog.

## light

```cpp
static Theme light()
```

Windows 11 Fluent, light: `fluent(Palette::fluent_light())`. The default theme a [Window](../tree/window.md) starts with, and the one to reach for in member defaults.

One [light()](#light) theme that lives as long as the program, the default argument where a control is measured or drawn on its own. Some containers keep a pointer to the theme they were last measured with, so a default made of a temporary would dangle.

## struct ControlSizing

[Control](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-control) density: the sizes compact density overrides. Each is nullopt in a standard theme, which leaves the control at its own standard size. [ControlSizing::compact()](#compact) holds the compact values, and ui/containers/DensityScope.hpp's [DensityScope](../layout/density-scope.md#uidensityscope) applies them to a subtree.

## struct SeverityVisual

Severity colors: [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar)'s icon disc and body, and [ProgressBar](../controls/progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)'s paused and error indicator. Read these instead of [`palette`](#palette), which only the Fluent themes fill.

The defaults are the Fluent light colors, so a theme that sets none still draws readable bars. [`Theme::fluent()`](#fluent) fills them from the palette, `resolve_high_contrast()` from the system's contrast colors, and an era theme sets its own where the era has them.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fill` | `Color` |  | the strong mark: [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar)'s icon disc, [ProgressBar](../controls/progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)'s indicator |
| `background` | `Color` |  | the surface behind the whole bar |

## struct Severities

The four [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar) severities plus the shared neutral fill, glyph and stroke colors.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `informational` | `SeverityVisual` | `{Color::from_argb(0xFF0078D4), Color::from_argb(0x80F6F6F6)}` | Drawn in the accent itself. [`Theme::fluent()`](#fluent) fills it from [`accent_button_normal`](#accent_button_normal). |
| `success` | `SeverityVisual` | `{Color::from_argb(0xFF0F7B0F), Color::from_argb(0xFFDFF6DD)}` | The success, caution and critical severities. |
| `caution` | `SeverityVisual` | `{Color::from_argb(0xFF9D5D00), Color::from_argb(0xFFFFF4CE)}` |  |
| `critical` | `SeverityVisual` | `{Color::from_argb(0xFFC42B1C), Color::from_argb(0xFFFDE7E9)}` |  |
| `neutral` | `Color` | `Color::from_argb(0xFF8A8A8A)` | The gray of [InfoBadge](../controls/info-badge.md#uiinfobadge)'s `Informational` styles. A fill only, since no [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar) severity is neutral. |
| `text_on_fill` | `Color` | `colors::White` | The glyph drawn on one of the `fill` discs, and the bar's own 1px outline. |
| `stroke` | `Color` | `Color::from_argb(0x0F000000)` |  |

### color_for_role

```cpp
const std::optional<Color>& color_for_role(TextRole role) const
```

The color for a [TextRole](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#textrole) (BodyStrong shares [`body`](#body)'s); unset means `colors.text`.

### struct RoleColors

Per-role foreground, for an era whose type ramp carries color as well as size and weight. Aero sets it: its main instruction is `#003399` Segoe UI 12pt and links are `#0066CC`. Every entry is unset for every other theme, so a role paints in [`ThemeColors::text`](theme-colors.md).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | `std::optional<Color>` |  | One optional color per role; unset paints in [`ThemeColors::text`](theme-colors.md). |
| `subheader` | `std::optional<Color>` |  |  |
| `title` | `std::optional<Color>` |  |  |
| `subtitle` | `std::optional<Color>` |  |  |
| `body` | `std::optional<Color>` |  |  |
| `caption` | `std::optional<Color>` |  |  |

## struct PageMetrics

Page layout metrics: the grid step, the page inset and header, and the item spacing. Metro sets its 20px grid and 120/140/50 page layout here; the defaults suit every other theme.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grid_unit` | `float` | `4.0f` | the layout grid step, in DIPs |
| `content_margin` | `Thickness` | `{12.0f}` | page content inset, in DIPs |
| `header_height` | `float` | `0.0f` | 0 == no header band |
| `item_spacing` | `float` | `4.0f` | gap between stacked items, in DIPs |
| `command_bar_height` | `float` | `48.0f` | a command bar's height, in DIPs |

## struct PopupMotion

How menus and drop-down lists open and close.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu` | `ThemePopupAnimation` | `ThemePopupAnimation::Slide` | how a menu opens |
| `list` | `ThemePopupAnimation` | `ThemePopupAnimation::None` | how a drop-down list opens |
| `open` | `Duration` | `{250.0}` | the opening animation's length |
| `close` | `Duration` | `{83.0}` | a menu's fade-out; 0 closes at once |
